findings: Exercise as printed on PDF 225-228 (printed pages 222-225): 10 MCQs, 9 short answer, 6 constructed response, 5 comprehensive questions and 10 numerical problems, each solved in English and Roman Urdu (MCQs as keyed checkpoints, the rest as self-checks with model answers; numericals worked step by step). Drafts for the academic review.
The book prints no MCQ key; keys were worked out from the chapter: 9.1 d, 9.2 b, 9.3 d, 9.4 d, 9.5 c, 9.6 c, 9.7 d, 9.8 d, 9.9 d, 9.10 b.
MCQ 9.2: strictly more than one option is a whole multiple of e (option (c) 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁵ C = 10⁴e); intended answer (b) 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁹ C = 2e. Book correction box added.
MCQ 9.3 relies on the printed field-line diagrams; they are described in words in the prompt.
MCQ 9.10 (radius of a charged particle's path in a magnetic field) is beyond this chapter; it is Chapter 10 work (r = mv/qB).
Numerical 9.9: the printed answer (4.8 GΩ, 2.4 × 10¹¹ J) is wrong; correct R = 47.8 Ω ≈ 48 Ω, heat ≈ 2.4 × 10³ J (taking 150 μm as the diameter). Book correction box added.

Numericals 9.7 and 9.8 print empty answer brackets; worked answers: R_Cu = 1.08 × 10⁻⁴ Ω, side of tungsten rod 1.52 cm; temperature rise ≈ 41 K (using the 20 °C resistance as reference; ≈ 44 K if reduced to 0 °C first, explained in a Wazahat box).

The scan is low resolution (595 × 770 px page images) and several small exponents are not legible: MCQ 9.2 (c), 9.4 options, 9.5 options; numericals 9.3 (r, answer), 9.4 (mass, answer), 9.5 (vᵢ, answer), 9.6 (E). Each was written as the value consistent with the printed mantissas and the printed answer (e.g. vᵢ = 2.99 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ gives the printed 3.34 × 10⁻⁸ s and 5.27 × 10¹³ m s⁻²). CRQ 9.3 is read as 10³⁶. Reviewer should confirm against the paper book.
Misprints kept as printed and explained: MCQ 9.4 "election", CRQ 9.5 "elections" (electrons), numerical 9.5 "filed" (field).

Answers beyond the chapter: short 9.1 (charging by friction of an aeroplane) and CRQ 9.5 (v_d = V/(nρeL), combining Eqs. 9.30-9.32) go a little beyond the chapter text. Comprehensive 9.3 uses the correct balance argument (B and D at the same potential) instead of the book's misprinted Eqs. 9.48-9.50; comprehensive 9.2 uses the corrected sign rules (lesson 9.16 book correction). Comprehensive 9.3 asks for a diagram: it is described in words (no figure added).
